o1.biggest_strength: It puts the cash where it matters: rush and standard orders for the top 5 matte shades, no money wasted on liquid or glitter, and a practical plan to move dead palette stock.
o1.biggest_mistake: It mishandles the re-cartoning math. Re-cartoning the 3,900 top-5 held units should lift top-5 stock to about 13,000 units and carry us to the rush delivery; the plan instead creates an unnecessary 1 to 7 December stockout/back-order gap.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fix the held-stock assumption and remove the false stockout plan, make the Monday PO dates fully consistent, and show the top-5 shade split clearly enough for ops to place the POs without interpretation.

o2.biggest_strength: It is very easy to act on: one Monday order table, clear dates, cash inside budget, and the right call to reject the ₹1.86 crore draft.
o2.biggest_mistake: It assumes the 3,900 held top-5 units are inside the 9,100 on hand, so it creates a false sellout gap and recommends pausing ads and capping orders when re-cartoning should largely prevent the gap.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Correct the held-stock math, show that re-cartoning gets us to the rush arrival, avoid unnecessary demand suppression, and sharpen the customer-facing copy into a bolder SUGAR voice.

reason: I would rather work from Output 1 because it has the stronger cash allocation logic, better slow-stock plan, and more commercial thinking. Output 2 is cleaner to read, but its false stockout response would make us slow sales at exactly the wrong time.
